test_title: PYST 17: RRB Group D - Mathematics (Held On: 04 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: maths
question: A water tank is initially one-tenth full. Pipe A can empty the tank in 6 minutes. After this, pipes A, B and C are opened together to fill the tank, where pipe B can fill it in 30 minutes and pipe C in 40 minutes. How long will it take to completely fill the tank?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Time for full tank (A) = 6 × 10 = 60 min (Emptying).

Let total capacity = LCM(60, 30, 40) = 120 units.

Efficiency A = 120 ÷ 60 = -2 units/min.

Efficiency B = 120 ÷ 30 = +4 units/min.

Efficiency C = 120 ÷ 40 = +3 units/min.

Combined Efficiency (A+B+C) = -2 + 4 + 3 = +5 units/min.

Time to fill = 120 ÷ 5 = 24 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 24 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Pipe A empties 1/10 tank in 6 min

⇒ full tank in 60 min.

Pipe B fills in 30 min,

Pipe C fills in 40 min.
